title: Potato tots, frozen, NS (fried or baked)

content.title: About
content.content: Potato tots are small, grated‑potato nuggets coated in a crisp breading and flash‑frozen for later preparation. They can be cooked by deep‑frying or baking, yielding a crunchy exterior and a soft interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tots are a staple side dish in fast‑food restaurants and school cafeterias.
Freezing locks in flavor and texture, allowing quick cooking at any time.
Gluten‑free versions use corn starch or rice flour for the coating.
In the United States they are known as "tater tots" and became popular in the 1950s.
Variants may include cheese, herbs, or vegetable blends.

items.title: Potassium source
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Despite heat processing, a modest amount of vitamin C remains, providing antioxidant protection.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: The starch in potatoes offers a steady release of energy, helping to maintain satiety.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: Compared with many snack foods, tots contain little simple sugar.

items.title: Fiber (when made with skin‑on potatoes)
items.content: If the tots are prepared from whole potatoes with skins, they add dietary fiber.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The breading and oil make tots calorie‑dense; portion control is important.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salty coatings increase sodium intake, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Standard tots contain wheat breading; those with celiac disease should choose gluten‑free options.

items.title: Trans fats (in some frying oils)
items.content: If deep‑fried in oils high in trans fats, they can negatively affect cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: For frying, heat oil to 180 °C and cook tots 3–4 minutes until golden. For baking, preheat oven to 200 °C, spread tots on a sheet and bake 15–20 minutes, turning halfway for even crispness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen tots in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. After opening the package, use within 3–4 months. Do not thaw beforehand; cook directly from frozen.
